title: Always on Top disables the window

judgment.rationale: The report has a complete activation sequence, cross-application reproduction, a fresh diagnostic archive, and a current Windows build. The symptom is specific enough for maintainer reproduction and module-level tracing.
evidence: Win-Ctrl-T activates Always on Top and leaves the affected window unable to receive mouse or keyboard input.
Window controls, scrolling, moving, and the toggle shortcut all fail.
The issue reproduces in Edge, Chrome, Git Bash, and Snipping Tool.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP was attached immediately after reproduction.
The report targets PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 on Windows 10.0.26200.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with Always on Top tracing and inspect the activation path for an unintended input-blocking or hit-test state applied to the target window.

fix_assessment.rationale: The symptom strongly indicates a PowerToys code issue, but a lightweight pass cannot safely identify whether the cause is an extended style, hit-test change, input capture, or foreground-window handling.

issue_context.summary: Activating Always on Top leaves otherwise normal windows non-interactive across several applications until the window is closed externally.
known_information: The reporter uses Win-Ctrl-T to activate Always on Top.
Mouse, keyboard, scrolling, window movement, and window controls stop working.
The toggle shortcut no longer works after activation.
The behavior reproduces across Edge, Chrome, Git Bash, and Snipping Tool.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached.
The report includes Windows 10.0.26200 and PowerToys 0.101.2362.0.
inferences: The cross-application scope points to a module-level window-style, hit-test, or input-routing problem rather than an application-specific bug.
The fact that the taskbar can close the window suggests the process remains alive while normal target-window interaction is blocked.
issue_context.analysis: The evidence is sufficient for a controlled maintainer reproduction and targeted tracing. Requesting another generic bug report would duplicate evidence already supplied.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, labels, automated triage comment, and attached diagnostic reference.
Confirmed the issue is cross-application and therefore suitable for module-level Always on Top investigation.

actions.label: Reproduce Always on Top input blocking

prerequisites: A normal interactive window such as Notepad, Edge, or Snipping Tool
Tracing or debugger access to the Always on Top activation path
steps: Open an ordinary interactive application window.
Press Win-Ctrl-T to enable Always on Top.
Try clicking the client area, title-bar buttons, and scrollable content.
Try typing and pressing Win-Ctrl-T again.
Repeat with Edge, Chrome, Git Bash, or Snipping Tool.
If interaction is lost, close the window from the taskbar and capture the applied window styles and hit-test/input state.
reproduce.expected_result: Always on Top changes z-order only; the target window continues to accept mouse and keyboard input and the shortcut can toggle the state off.
setup_requirements: Compare the target window styles and input state before and after activation.
Record whether the failure occurs before or after the window is raised.
